text: You click *BUY*. 2 seconds later, order executed. Easy, right?
Actually, *6 institutions* just worked for you.
Number one is your *broker*. It checks you have the money and sends your order to the exchange. Number two is the *exchange*: NSE or BSE.
Its computer finds a seller at your price and matches you in a fraction of a second.
It becomes the buyer to the seller and the seller to the buyer, and *guarantees* the trade even if a broker defaults.
Number four is the *depository*: NSDL or CDSL.
It moves the shares into your demat account.
Number five is the *bank*: it moves your money. And number six is *SEBI*, the regulator,
which watches all the activities of all the parties involved in the stock market.
India settles in *T+1*: the shares you buy today, you will get in your demat account tomorrow.
So the next time you tap BUY, remember: it's not an app, it's a *relay race*. The full story is on the channel.
If you want such practical finance every day,
Do *like, share and subscribe*. Thank you so much.
